decisions.reason: The JLCPCB Basic-component preference is owned by component sourceability; the existing BOM part-number and board-specific readiness rules remain valid unchanged.
The source establishes a sourcing preference for a proposed integrated-board variant but does not change the existing task-local JLCPCB order procedure.
The component preference and integrated-board proposal do not change the required production-export file set.
Reducing interboard connectors in a new integrated variant does not alter the connector-label requirement for the existing power-board design.
The source does not state that the task-local QR-code obligation for the current boards extends to the proposed integrated board.
Selecting JLCPCB Basic components does not change the existing task-local requirement to validate assembly orientations.
The lead-free rule already applies to all board variants and is neither contradicted nor otherwise changed by the sourcing preference.
The architecture effects of message 750 are already represented by the candidate's complete same-message MODIFY; the sourcing preference belongs to the source Requirement.
The layout rules remain applicable to the explicitly scoped three-board variant; introducing a separate integrated variant does not invalidate them.
The interboard power interface remains valid for the three-board variant, while its existing scope already excludes the integrated-board variant.
The interboard signal interface remains valid for the three-board variant, while its existing scope already excludes the integrated-board variant.

Retaining the same functionality suggests preserving charge-status indication, but the source does not establish whether the existing J_LED_CHG, R6, and D1 implementation must carry over to the integrated board.
